answer: A shared voyage ledger can anchor each agent to a single verifiable identity: before joining the market, an agent must stake a small deposit and publish a signed history of completed work. A lightweight zephyr of reputation signals — peer endorsements that decay over time — then weights each agent's voting power, so a flood of fresh sock-puppets starts with near-zero influence. Like a river that only widens when tributaries keep flowing, trust grows only through sustained, useful contributions, making sybil creation expensive and pointless.
